comment: The slash-command list a phone offers for a terminal pane. Rows are seeded from a live 2026-08-20 read of the pinned pair (Claude Code 2.1.233 / Agent SDK 0.3.233) via supportedCommands(), which reported 138 commands on the owner's Mac: a built-in with an argument hint, one carrying the vendor's aliases (/cost and /stats both resolve to /usage), a plugin-namespaced skill reachable by its unprefixed shorthand, one with no description at all, and one hand-kept terminal-only command the vendor advertises nowhere. Descriptions here are already clipped to the wire bound; the vendor's own run past 400 bytes. Every entry under refused_* is annotated in `why` alongside the frame. Unknown *keys* are skipped by consumers rather than refused, so a newer host cannot delete the feature on an older app; unknown or malformed *values* are still refused whole.

commands.name: compact
commands.description: Summarize the conversation so far and free up context

commands.name: usage
commands.description: Show plan usage limits and current consumption

commands.name: exit
commands.description: Leave Claude Code and return to the shell

empty_response_comment: Every reason the host cannot vouch for a list looks identical on the wire: no agent in the pane, an agent that is not Claude, no managed runtime installed, a probe that timed out. The phone shows no picker for all of them and never learns which.

refused_requests.why: A plain shell has no multiplexer to ask, so it is refused rather than answered empty.
An agent route names no provider either.
A session name outside the §5.4 alphabet never reaches a provider argv.

refused_responses.why: A command name carrying whitespace would be typed into a terminal as two words.
A name is an identifier; a slash inside one names a path, not a command.
An empty name would render as a bare slash.
A control byte in display text is refused even though the name is fine.
